origin: The regional claims are accurate (Atlantic side lowest for the date, Greenland and Barents 30% below the previous low, Hudson Bay and the Canadian Arctic Archipelago lowest since 1979, open water about 400 miles from the Pole). "This is what burning fossil fuels does" is mainstream attribution of the long-term decline. Overstatement: "this September, Arctic sea ice will smash the 2012 record low." The fact sheet has Arctic-wide extent 6th lowest and about 1% above the same date in 2025 (which ended tied tenth lowest, 1.21 million square kilometers above 2012), and the Pacific side unusually icy. Expected honest rating: 50 to 65 (drafter's range, set with the Met Office outlook on the fact sheet; without it the start may sit toward the top of the range).

evidence_down.evidence_note: Real. NSIDC, "Arctic sea ice minimum ties for tenth lowest", published 2026-09-23 (date from the NSIDC analyses index datetime, src/nsidc-analyses.html), https://nsidc.org/sea-ice-today/analyses/arctic-sea-ice-minimum-ties-tenth-lowest-0 (src/nsidc-min-2026.md). Verbatim: "On September 12, Arctic sea ice likely reached its annual minimum extent of 4.60 million square kilometers (1.78 million square miles). The 2026 minimum shares the tenth lowest spot in the nearly 48-year satellite record with 2008, 2010, and 2025." "It is 1.21 million square kilometers (467,000 square miles) above the satellite-era record minimum extent of 3.39 million square kilometers (1.31 million square miles), which occurred on September 17, 2012". "In the 48-year-satellite record, the 20 lowest minimums have all occurred in the last 20 years." "The overall, downward trend in the minimum extent from 1979 to 2026 is 11.8 percent per decade relative to the 1981 to 2010 average." "This overall trend should be viewed with the caveat that there has been no significant decline in September minimum extents over the past two decades." "Note that this is a preliminary announcement."
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: on September 23, 2026, the National Snow and Ice Data Center reported that Arctic sea ice likely reached its 2026 minimum extent on September 12, at 4.60 million square kilometers. That ties 2008, 2010 and 2025 for the tenth lowest minimum in the nearly 48-year satellite record and is 1.21 million square kilometers above the record low of 3.39 million square kilometers set in 2012. NSIDC notes that the 20 lowest minimums have all occurred in the last 20 years, that the downward trend from 1979 to 2026 is 11.8 percent per decade, and that there has been no significant decline in September minimum extents over the past two decades. The announcement is preliminary. Does that change your rating?
Makes sense. What is your final number?
